CASE STUDY

I ran an agent on 100 apps. Here is how well it did.

A research agent researched the API, auth, and buildability surface of 100 apps for the Composio take-home. Checked against 20 apps whose gold answers were drafted from official docs (I verified 15 of 20 myself), it got about half of the checks right. A second pass added a verify-and-retry loop that made the evidence better grounded — it did not make the answers more accurate.

Overall: 53/107 → 53/107, 49.5% → 49.5%, no change. No improvement is claimed. The 9 gold apps whose pass 1 record also came from Gemini went from 29/49 to 31/49 — 2 more correct answers, too few to call an improvement.

8 regressions:

  • DealCloud/api_type, Zendesk/api_type, Sherlock/api_type, WhatsApp Business/auth_methods, PitchBook/auth_methods — in all five, pass 2 added an extra value to a list field; the exact-set scoring rule marks the whole field wrong even though the original correct value is still there; the extra values were not checked one by one.
  • fanbasis/auth_methods and fanbasis/access — correct in pass 1, unknown in pass 2. A real loss: fanbasis's real docs are on commasdocs.com, a different domain from its product site, and pass 2's search missed that domain again, the same way pass 1's did.
  • Waterfall.io/access — unknown in pass 1, a specific (wrong, per gold) guess in pass 2.
The loop

What the verify and retry loop changed

Apps failing each check, pass 1 (45 apps) vs pass 2 (50 apps). The loop enforces these same checks, so this shows evidence is better grounded. It is not a measure of whether the final answers are more accurate.

29 → 2
Quote is on the page (D1)
better
13 → 0
Source is trusted (D2)
better
1 → 0
Page loaded OK (D3)
better
8 → 14
Fields agree with each other (D4)
worse

Pass 1 only has 45 of the 50 apps here, not 50, because the other 5 failed outright and have no pass 1 record. D1–D3 improved sharply, which is what the retry loop is for. D4 got worse: D4 checks three rules, not only MCP URLs — access/buildability, api_type/main_blocker, and existing_mcp_status/existing_mcp_url. On the 45 apps present in both passes, pass 1 had 21 apps with existing_mcp_status official/community (7 of those missing a URL); pass 2 had 20 (11 missing a URL) — accounting for the shared-45-app rise (8 → 11 failing). The rest of the jump to 14 comes from 3 of the 5 apps pass 1 never researched at all (Xero, Fathom, Reducto), which pass 2 also flagged as official/community with no URL. So the URL counts explain the whole rise within the shared 45 apps, but only part of the 8-to-14 figure above, which compares different app counts. Pass 2 is not claiming official/community more often overall; it is more likely to leave the URL missing when it does make that claim. The cause was not measured.

Human review

Human review of 8 apps

I checked 13 fields on 8 apps against vendor pages and search results: HubSpot, Close, Copper, GitHub, Notion, Jira, Linear and Clay. The agent had flagged 7 of the 8 (HubSpot and Close existing_mcp; unknown existing_mcp for GitHub, Notion, Jira, Linear, Clay). Copper was not flagged.

  • Wrong or missed (6): Copper existing_mcp "none" (an official server is announced but not public yet, and third-party servers exist); existing_mcp "unknown" for GitHub, Notion, Jira, Linear and Clay, where an official server exists for each.
  • Unproven or weak (3): Close access "paid_plan_required" (the pricing page shows a free trial that seems to include API access; one FAQ answer was not fully read); Close "bearer_token" (the API key page says HTTP Basic; the OAuth page was not opened); HubSpot's single "public beta" quote used for 3 fields (an old changelog post).
  • Held up (4): HubSpot official MCP, Close official MCP, Copper auth methods, HubSpot bearer_token (a Bearer header, but not a separate method).

For the five "unknown" apps I looked at Google results, not the vendors' own pages, so server URLs are not confirmed. URLs for HubSpot and Close were not found on the pages I opened. These apps were picked because they were flagged or looked doubtful, so the counts are not an error rate for all 50 apps. The data files were not changed. Notes are in data/human_review_notes.md.

Limitations

Limitations and next steps

  • 49 of 95 researched apps have at least one unknown/low-confidence field (147 such fields total) — these are gaps the agent admitted to, not silent guesses.
  • Accuracy on the gold set is 49.5% in both pass 1 and pass 2 — well short of production quality. The verify/retry loop in pass 2 did not improve it.
  • qwen/qwen3.8-27b's records are markedly less reliable than the other two models — a direct consequence of switching providers mid-run under free-tier quota pressure, not a reflection of the agent design.
  • 5 apps have no record at all (not researched), all due to LLM provider errors during extraction, not missing data on the web.
  • D1 only checks that the evidence quote exists on the page it cites — it does not check that the quote actually supports the field's value. A real quote next to a wrong conclusion still passes.
  • List fields can pick up extra values. Exact-set scoring marks the whole field as a miss. The extra values were not checked one by one, so some may be wrong.
  • An unknown api_breadth or unknown existing_mcp_status can never trigger a retry under the current checks, by construction, not bad luck. Of the fields left unknown after pass 2, 31 were never retried for this reason.
  • The gold set is small: 20 apps total, and only 7 of them have a verified existing_mcp_status label, so the existing_mcp_status numbers above are on a thin sample.
  • No flag does not mean correct: Copper's existing_mcp was none with no evidence and no flag, and it was wrong. All 5 unknown MCP values checked by hand were findable.
  • The agent's own catalog check never ran. The catalog check above was done separately, by name, so it shows that a toolkit exists, not how complete it is.

Next steps (planned, not done yet)

  • Let unknown api_breadth and existing_mcp_status fields trigger a retry.
  • Check that each value in a list field has its own supporting quote.
  • Look for docs on a different domain than the product site (the fanbasis case).
  • Review the rest of the 29 flagged apps and the low-confidence fields, and re-score.
  • Run pass 2 on the other 50 apps when quota allows.

App integration research agent · pass 1 + pass 2 (50 of 100 apps)

Generated 2026-11-23 17:04 UTC. Pass 1 models: gemini-3.5-flash-lite (48 apps), openai/gpt-oss-120b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b. Groq API calls (exact, from the usage tracker): 126. Gemini calls: not instrumented exactly — at least 2 per completed Gemini app (~96), excluding retries.

Pass 2 (Gemini only, no fallback): about 310 Gemini requests (counted by the pipeline) across 50 apps, including retries. 12 real 429s occurred, all absorbed by Google's client-side retry.

Pass 1 covers 100 apps; pass 2 covers 50 of them; a partial human review of 8 apps was done (see "Human review of 8 apps"), the rest of the flagged apps are not reviewed.
